mainTopic: Buying שביעית produce from an עם הארץ: the three-meal limit, ownerless versus guarded produce, and whether the לולב and אתרוג count as שביעית produce
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about paying an עם הארץ with money that carries קדושת שביעית. You may give him only enough for three meals, and only for produce from an ownerless (מופקר) field. Produce from a guarded (משומר) field may not be bought from him at all. רב ששת challenges this from a משנה that allows buying wild plants 'from any person'. He answers that the משנה also means only a food-amount (כדי מן), and רבי יוחנן says the same. The גמרא proves from a פסוק in דניאל that 'מן' means food. The גמרא then asks why the same rule does not forbid buying a לולב, and answers that the לולב grew in the sixth year. It asks the same about the אתרוג and answers that an אתרוג follows its picking. The גמרא challenges this from a משנה in ביכורים, which says that for שביעית an אתרוג follows tree rules (budding). The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the instruction: he eats his own produce with שביעית sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its instruction. The buyer goes home and eats his own produce, which now carries the קדושת שביעית that was moved off the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he comes home and eats that produce with the holiness of the Seventh Year.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא, which began on the previous amud, is finishing its instruction. The buyer must treat his own produce at home as holy שביעית food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money paid for שביעית produce takes on קדושת שביעית. Before he pays the עם הארץ, the buyer transfers that holiness from the coins onto produce in his own house. As a result, it is the buyer's own produce, not the money in the hands of the עם הארץ, that must be eaten with the rules of שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The special holiness of Seventh-Year produce and of the money used to buy it
And he eats them
The Seventh (Sabbatical) Year

phrases.english: And he comes and eats them
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to the produce in his own house, onto which the holiness of the money was transferred.

phrases.english: with the sanctity of the Seventh Year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The holiness is transferred to the buyer's own produce, and he eats that produce with קדושת שביעית.

steps.title: The three-meal permission applies only to ownerless produce
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the three-meal permission to produce taken from a מופקר field. If the produce came from a guarded (משומר) field, even a tiny amount like half an איסר is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? When he buys from produce that was left ownerless. But if he buys from produce that was guarded, even half an איסר's worth is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now limits its own rule. It tells us exactly when the three-meal allowance applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית, a field must be left open to everyone (מופקר). Produce from such a field is permitted, so the only concern is how the עם הארץ will use the money, and three meals' worth is tolerated. Produce from a field the owner illegally guarded (משומר) is itself problematic, so any purchase at all is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (a formula that introduces a limitation)
Ownerless; left open for anyone to take
Guarded; kept for the owner, against the law of שביעית
About half an איסר, a very small coin

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast that רב ששת's question depends on: ownerless produce has a limit of three meals. Is that limit really there?

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
When one buys from ownerless produce.
But when one buys from guarded produce,
even for about half an issar, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the ברייתא's three-meal rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three-meal allowance applies only to produce from a מופקר field. Produce from a משומר field may not be bought from an עם הארץ at all.

steps.title: רב ששת challenges the three-meal limit from a משנה about wild plants
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת asks: is ownerless produce really limited to three meals? A משנה in שביעית says wild plants may be bought 'from any person' with no limit mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: Is ownerless produce limited to three meals and no more? A source contradicts this. 'Rue, sorrel, asparagus, purslane, mountain coriander, river water-parsley, and field-eruca are exempt from tithes. They may be bought from any person in the Seventh Year, because plants of their kind are never guarded.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the ברייתא's three-meal limit. He quotes a משנה that seems to allow buying ownerless wild plants from anyone, in any amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These plants grow wild and nobody guards them, so they are like מופקר produce. The משנה says they can be bought 'מכל אדם', which includes an עם הארץ, and it mentions no three-meal cap. This seems to contradict the ברייתא, which allows only three meals' worth even for מופקר produce.

keyTerms.meaning: And no more?
And they contradicted it (a contradiction from another source)
From any person, including an עם הארץ
Exempt from tithes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה is talking about guarded produce. Its whole point is that these plants are never guarded, so they belong in the same 'ownerless' category as the ברייתא's case. That is exactly why there is a contradiction.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objected:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַמּוּפְקָר שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת וְתוּ לָא?
phrases.english: And from ownerless produce, only three meals and no more?
And a source contradicts this:
Rue, sorrel, and asparagus,
purslane, and coriander of the mountains,
water parsley of the rivers, and eruca of the field,
are exempt from tithes,
and may be bought from any person in the Seventh Year,
because nothing of their kind is guarded.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the three-meal limit for מופקר produce stated in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that even ownerless produce may be bought from an עם הארץ only up to three meals' worth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in שביעית allows buying wild, unguarded plants 'from any person' and mentions no quantity limit. This implies there is no three-meal cap on ownerless produce.

steps.title: רב ששת answers himself: the משנה also means a food-amount
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת resolves his own question. The משנה was taught about buying only 'כדי מן', a food-sized amount, so the three-meal limit still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised the objection and he answered it: they taught this only for an amount enough for food.
steps.whatsHappening: The same רב ששת who asked the question now answers it. He reads a hidden limit into the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only means that these plants can be bought even from an עם הארץ, since nobody suspects they were guarded. It does not mean any amount is allowed. The limit of 'כדי מן', food for three meals, still applies, so the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection and he himself resolved it
In an amount enough for food (sustenance)
They taught

phrases.aramaic: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ:
phrases.english: He raised the objection and he resolved it:
They taught it regarding an amount sufficient for sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה: an unstated quantity cap is read into it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows buying unlimited amounts of wild plants from anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה allows buying from anyone, but only up to a food-amount (three meals), just like the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the same answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן the identical answer, 'בכדי מן שנו', which supports רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: they taught it regarding an amount enough for food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב ששת's answer. A major authority, רבי יוחנן, said the exact same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law here. The point is that רב ששת's reading of the משנה is not his own invention, because רבי יוחנן independently said the same thing. This strengthens the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said (a formula that introduces matching support)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And so said Rabba bar bar Ḥana
in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
They taught it regarding an amount sufficient for sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's reading that the משנה is limited to 'כדי מן'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's identical statement, transmitted by רבה בר בר חנה.

steps.title: How do we know 'מן' means food?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that the word 'מן' refers to food or sustenance.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see that this word 'מן' is a word for food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the meaning of a word. This sets up the next step, which brings a proof from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer depends on reading 'מן' as 'food', not as the ordinary Hebrew 'from'. So the גמרא wants a source showing this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied?
A term meaning food or sustenance

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this word 'man' is a term for sustenance?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי מָן לִישָּׁנָא דִּמְזוֹנֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the key word used in the answer of steps 4-5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that 'מן' means food.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק in דניאל: 'וימן להם המלך'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from דניאל 1:5, 'וימן להם המלך', that the king appointed food portions, so the root 'מן' relates to sustenance.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the king appointed (וימן) for them...' a daily portion of the king's food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the word question with a פסוק. The verb 'וימן' is used for giving out food portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, the king assigned the young men a daily ration from his food, and the verb used is 'וימן'. This shows that the root 'מן' is connected to providing food. So 'כדי מן' means 'enough for food', the three-meal amount.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
And he appointed or allotted (food portions)
Etc.: the verse continues

steps.whatToRemember: Ownerless (מופקר) שביעית produce may be bought from an עם הארץ only up to a food-amount, three meals. Guarded (משומר) produce may not be bought from him at all. The משנה that allows wild plants 'from anyone' still keeps the 'כדי מן' limit, and 'מן' means food, as in 'וימן להם המלך'.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the king appointed for them, etc."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse in דניאל 1:5 uses 'וימן' for allotting food, so 'מן' means sustenance.

steps.title: Then why not forbid buying the לולב too?
steps.stepSummary: If we may not hand an עם הארץ money for שביעית produce, buying a לולב from him should be forbidden as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then a לולב should also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the משנה. If we cannot pay an עם הארץ for שביעית produce, why does the משנה let us buy the לולב from him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained that we cannot give an עם הארץ money for שביעית produce beyond a food-sized amount. The משנה only worried about the אתרוג. The גמרא asks why the same worry does not apply to the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: a challenge that takes the last answer and pushes it further
The palm branch taken on סוכות
Also, too

phrases.english: If so, a lulav too [should be forbidden]!
phrases.notes: If paying for שביעית produce is the problem, the לולב should be a problem as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the established rule about paying an עם הארץ for שביעית produce and applies it to the לולב in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's distinction between buying a לולב and buying an אתרוג from an עם הארץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is the ban on paying for שביעית produce, the לולב should fall under the same ban.

steps.title: The לולב grew in the sixth year
steps.stepSummary: The לולב in the משנה grew in the sixth year and only stayed into the seventh, so it is not שביעית produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לולב is from the sixth year and is only entering the seventh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this לולב has no שביעית holiness at all. It grew in the sixth year, so paying for it is no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכות comes only a few days after ראש השנה. A לולב used on סוכות at the start of the seventh year grew in the sixth year. Because a לולב follows the time it grew, it counts as sixth-year produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Belonging to the sixth year
Entering into the seventh year
The seventh (Sabbatical) year, when produce has special holiness

phrases.aramaic: לוּלָב בַּר שִׁשִּׁית הַנִּכְנָס לִשְׁבִיעִית הוּא.
phrases.english: The lulav is of the sixth year that is entering the seventh.
phrases.notes: It grew before ראש השנה, so it has no שביעית holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוּלָב בַּר שִׁשִּׁית הַנִּכְנָס לִשְׁבִיעִית הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by explaining that the לולב in question is sixth-year produce.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition: the לולב is from the sixth year, so it has no שביעית status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the לולב was שביעית produce, just like the אתרוג.
steps.terutzMaskana: The לולב grew in the sixth year, so paying the עם הארץ for it is permitted.

steps.title: The אתרוג also grew in the sixth year
steps.stepSummary: If so, the אתרוג should also count as sixth-year produce that has entered the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the אתרוג too is from the sixth year and is only entering the seventh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer against itself. The אתרוג on the tree at סוכות also grew in the sixth year, so it should also be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 depended on when the plant grew. An אתרוג used at the start of the seventh year also formed during the sixth year. So the משנה's distinction between the two still needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The citron fruit taken on סוכות
Belonging to the sixth year (feminine form, describing the אתרוג)

phrases.english: If so, an etrog too —
it is of the sixth year that is entering the seventh!
phrases.notes: It uses the same wording as the לולב answer, now applied to the אתרוג.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 9 and shows it should apply equally to the אתרוג.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the לולב is sixth-year produce, and the משנה's different treatment of the אתרוג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If growing in the sixth year frees the לולב, the אתרוג also grew in the sixth year and should be free too.

steps.title: For an אתרוג we follow the time of picking
steps.stepSummary: An אתרוג's year is set by when it is picked, not when it grew, so an אתרוג picked in the seventh year is שביעית produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an אתרוג, we go by the time of its picking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the אתרוג is different from the לולב. Its year depends on when it was picked, so an אתרוג picked after ראש השנה counts as seventh-year produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is how vegetables work: their year follows their picking (לקיטה). The answer treats the אתרוג like a vegetable for this purpose. That explains why the משנה forbids paying for the אתרוג but not for the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: After, according to
Picking, harvesting
We go (by), we follow

phrases.english: An etrog — we go after the picking.
phrases.notes: Its year is set by when it was picked, the way vegetables work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by giving the אתרוג a different rule for setting its year.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the אתרוג follows picking, unlike the לולב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אתרוג follows the time it grew, just like the לולב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אתרוג follows its picking, so one picked in the seventh year is שביעית produce.

steps.title: Both תנאים agree the אתרוג follows budding for שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר disagree elsewhere, but both agree that for שביעית an אתרוג follows its budding (חנטה), not its picking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But both according to רבן גמליאל and according to רבי אליעזר, regarding שביעית we go by the budding of the אתרוג!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 11. Everyone agrees that for שביעית the אתרוג follows its budding, so the answer seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר argue about the אתרוג for the laws of מעשרות. For שביעית, though, both agree it follows חנטה, the time the fruit first forms, which is the rule for trees. If so, an אתרוג that formed in the sixth year should be sixth-year produce, and the problem from step 10 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely: opens a challenge based on a known fact
Budding, the first forming of the fruit
With regard to, for the purpose of

steps.confusionAlert: The argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר is about מעשרות. For שביעית they agree. The גמרא brings both names to show that no one holds the אתרוג follows picking for שביעית.

phrases.english: But surely, both according to Rabban Gamliel
and according to Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: They argue about the אתרוג for מעשרות.

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן שְׁבִיעִית אֶתְרוֹג בָּתַר חֲנָטָה אָזְלִינַן!
phrases.english: regarding the Sabbatical Year, for an etrog we go after the budding!
phrases.notes: This is the tree rule, which contradicts step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּין רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּבֵין רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11 using a rule that all agree on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that for an אתרוג we follow the time of picking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions agree that for שביעית an אתרוג follows budding, so it cannot follow picking for שביעית.

steps.title: משנה: the אתרוג is like a tree in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in ביכורים: an אתרוג is like a tree in three ways and like a vegetable in one way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: an אתרוג is like a tree in three ways, and like a vegetable in one way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up its challenge. It quotes a משנה that sorts out when the אתרוג acts like a tree and when it acts like a vegetable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trees follow budding (חנטה) and vegetables follow picking (לקיטה). The משנה says the אתרוג is mostly treated like a tree. The next step shows that שביעית is one of the tree ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Is like a tree (in its laws)
Vegetable
Ways, respects

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים,
phrases.english: As we learned: An etrog is like a tree in three ways,
and like a vegetable in one way.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אֶתְרוֹג שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 12 that for שביעית an אתרוג follows budding.

steps.title: The three tree ways include שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the three tree ways: ערלה, רבעי, and שביעית. It then begins to name the one vegetable way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like a tree in three ways: for ערלה, for רבעי, and for שביעית. And like a vegetable in one way:
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה spells out its list, and שביעית is one of the tree ways. The sentence about the vegetable way is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שביעית is on the tree list, the אתרוג follows budding for שביעית. That directly contradicts step 11, which said we follow picking. The one vegetable way, coming next, is where picking matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Fourth-year fruit, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed
One

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the clear source that the אתרוג follows tree rules for שביעית. The סוגיא, continuing on the next amud, has to explain how step 11 can still stand.

phrases.english: It is like a tree in three ways —
phrases.notes: The משנה now explains its own list.

phrases.english: for orlah, for fourth-year fruit, and for the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: שביעית is on the tree list, so it follows budding.

phrases.english: And like a vegetable in one way —
phrases.notes: This continues on the next amud (the answer is מעשרות).

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁוֶה לָאִילָן בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים לְעׇרְלָה וְלִרְבָעִי וְלִשְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה, spelling out the three tree ways and showing that שביעית is one of them.
steps.raayaObject: That for שביעית an אתרוג follows budding, which contradicts step 11.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The detailed list in משנה ביכורים 2:6.
